reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that: the redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment was proposed, so nothing is being raised in negotiation.

The cited text supports compliance — Section 3.1 is a plain engagement of Cellco as Servicer with no 'exclusive', 'sole supplier' or requirements-purchase language binding the Issuer/Depositor, and Section 7.4/p0335 confirms the appointment can be terminated and replaced by a Successor Servicer, so there is no term-length lock-in or performance-exit gap.

Rationale correctly distinguishes non-exclusivity-related uses of 'sole'/'exclusive' (sole remedy, sole discretion, non-exclusive jurisdiction, Cap Collateral Account control) and notes the structural single-servicer appointment is not an exclusive dealing covenant; this reaches the preferred position, not merely the fallback.
Deterministic check ('no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains') passes, corroborating the assessment; no actionable edit is required or expected for a compliant finding.
